top_signal.title: Being sued as a small business owner — what happens when you can’t afford to fight back?
top_signal.summary: I run a very small online business selling products on Amazon. Recently, my company was sued in DC over a pocket square that cost only a few dollars.   The lawsuit alleges that the product’s actual fabric composition did not match the material described in the online listing, and that the product did not have the required fiber content and other labeling information. The plaintiff has offered to settle for $10,000 plus additional terms.   I understand that product labeling laws are important, and I take these allegations seriously. I am not saying my company is automatically right. But the settlement demand and the potential cost of legal representation have been overwhelming for a business as small as mine.   The hardest part is feeling that the other side understands the legal system far better than I do, while I may not even be able to afford the legal help needed to defend my company.   I have been struggling with depression while trying to keep my business running and take care of my family. This situation has made an already difficult time much harder.   While searching the DC Superior Court database, I found several other cases filed by the same organization that were listed as open at the time I checked. I also found articles discussing similar consumer protection lawsuits against online retailers and the financial pressure they can create for small businesses.
